stage1.impression: A clean, coherent night composition. The rim-lit globe reads as the hero and its six coloured rims are crisp, and the lamp halo in the haze is believable. Everything around it says CG, though: the far facades are flat brown slabs with identical emissive window cards and no brick, the paving is a uniform tile, the bollards are copies of one model, the plinth is a black hole, and the whole frame sits in one orange cast with no night-blue anywhere. A jury would see a specific, striking work, but in a generic render of a place, not a photograph of the Amsterdam canals.

blocking_9: The far houses read as real Amsterdam canal houses: brick with mortar and weathering, varied gables, window frames with mullions, and lit windows that show curtains or interiors at varied warm intensities instead of flat uniform cards
The frame holds a night-blue component (sky, water, unlit stone) against the warm practicals; b_median on the facade at 12 or more instead of 6
The globe's coloured shadow is plainly visible and legible on the paving as a separate image of the work
The plinth shows its blackened-steel sheen and edges (median 18 or more), not a crushed silhouette
The rims' colour shows up in the paving and water as reflections or spill, which ties the work into the site
Street props are varied and show life (a parked bicycle, distant figures, bollards that are not identical copies), and the paving and kerb have stone texture and wear

defects.what: Facades are flat untextured brown planes. Windows are uniform emissive rectangles with no depth, mullions or interiors. The houses read as a modern block with a few step-gable silhouettes, not canal houses
Unlit dark pole in front of the facade reads as a floating pipe (likely a far-quay lamp mast with no lamp)
Second unlit dark pole, same problem
Plinth crushed to near black (lum_median 9), with no steel sheen or edge definition
The globe's coloured shadow is faint and muddy: a pale pinkish disc with no legible coloured rings
Three bollards are identical copies of one glossy red-brown model with plastic highlights
Paving is a uniform clean tile with no stone variation, joints wear or wet sheen. The kerb edge is a plain CG step
Water reflects only the windows. No reflection of the globe's rims or the lamp, and the ripple is uniform
Visible grain/noise on the dark facade at 1:1
Orange meridian reads as pale pink/peach and the violet as pale lavender-blue under the AgX grade. Colours look desaturated against the stated palette
Monochrome orange grade: b_median 2 to 8 in every region, and no cool sky or night-blue anywhere

changes.problem: The houses across the canal are flat brown slabs with card windows, which reads as a game backdrop, not Amsterdam.

evidence.measured: facade wall areas are flat (no texture at 1:1), and lit windows are uniform flat fills (crop at 2x)

change.setting: the houses across: brick material and window assets
change.from: flat brown diffuse, windows as flat emissive panes, 0.35 lit at glow 0.08
change.to: dark red-brown brick with mortar and soot variation, white-painted window frames with mullions and inset depth, lit windows 0.35 with glow randomised 0.03 to 0.15 at 2400 to 3000 K, half of them behind curtains or with an interior back-plane

changes.expected: The facades read as real canal houses. Windows vary in brightness and colour, and the walls show texture.

changes.problem: Everything sits in one orange cast with no night-blue, so the frame reads as a graded render rather than a night photograph, and the rims' colours wash toward pink.

evidence.measured: b_median 6, r_median 38; paving b_median 18 vs r 78; globe region b_median 8

change.to: white_balance_k 4200, sky a deep-blue night gradient at strength 0.12

changes.expected: Practicals stay warm while the sky, water and unlit stone pick up a blue tint, and the rims' hues separate more cleanly.

changes.problem: The globe's coloured shadow, the image's second idea, is barely visible on the paving.

evidence.measured: lum_median 60, lum_range 69.5; the rings are not legible as colours

change.to: 700 W, cone 14 deg, 4000 K, aimed at [0.6, -2.2, 0.0], and haze from 0.004 to 0.0025 per metre

changes.expected: A crisp coloured shadow of the six rings lands on the paving beside the plinth, with clear dark/light contrast.

changes.problem: The plinth is crushed to black, so the work's base has no material.

change.from: blackened steel, near-matte; lit only by the spot's spill
change.to: blackened steel at roughness 0.35 with a brownish uneven sheen, plus a low 2400 K bounce card or quay fill at 0.8 W/m2 toward the plinth's front

changes.expected: The plinth reads as dark steel with a soft sheen on its curved face and a defined top edge catching the rims' colour.

changes.problem: The quay's paving and the water don't show the work's light, so the globe looks pasted onto the scene.

evidence.measured: water lum_p95 81 with only window reflections; no coloured rim reflections in water or on the paving

change.setting: paving and water finish; the rims' glow
change.from: dry uniform tile; water gloss as now; rim emission 0.18
change.to: damp brick/basalt setts with roughness varying 0.3 to 0.7 and worn joints; water roughness 0.05 with finer ripple; rim emission 0.25

changes.expected: Soft coloured streaks of the rims appear in the damp paving and the canal surface, and the paving shows stone texture.

changes.problem: Bollards are identical copies with plastic highlights, and there is no sign of life on the quay.

evidence.measured: visual: three matching glossy red-brown cylinders

change.from: identical glossy bollards, no people or bicycles
change.to: Amsterdammertje-style dark cast-iron bollards with varied wear and matte paint, a parked bicycle against the far left railing, two or three soft distant figures on the far quay

changes.expected: The quay reads as an inhabited Amsterdam street, and props no longer look duplicated.

changes.problem: Two unlit poles in front of the far facade read as floating pipes.

evidence.measured: visual: dark vertical cylinders with no lamp heads

change.to: matching lantern heads lit at 60 W, 2200 K, or remove the poles

changes.expected: The far quay gets small warm practicals that reflect in the water, and the stray pipes disappear.

changes.problem: Grain on the dark facade reads as render noise rather than film.

evidence.measured: visible speckle on flat wall at 2x crop

changes.expected: Clean dark tones, so any added grain can be a deliberate film grain.

out_of_scope.request: Make the orange meridian read clearly orange and the violet clearly violet; under the current grade they look peach and lavender
out_of_scope.why: The disc colours are fixed. Only the grade (c2) and emission level may help, so if hue error persists, check the material hexes against the design.

out_of_scope.request: Show the clear disc faces as thick polished acrylic with visible edge glow on the face and clean reflections; they currently read as faint smoky planes
out_of_scope.why: Disc thickness and the rim-lit/clear-face design are fixed.
